notes: Seven invalidate, two keep. Corrections to the pre-read: (1) ownership-history's duckdb-native SQL does not ignore cdc_flag -- it never reads raw.customer_cdc or raw.account_cdc at all (both .sql files read only raw.customer_mgmt_action), so the flag is unreachable there; the withdrawn-record-stays-current behavior the CE describes is a property of the L2 model's declared CDC handoffs, all of which are still deferred under L1.hole.change-effective-time. (2) trade-lifecycle does not filter D out wholesale: only latest_outcome does (cdc_flag IN ('I','U')). valid_cdc_rows, and hence first_cdc_report, first_report, placed_at, owning_account_number, order_type and first_seen_late, admit D. So a D-only trade currently DOES get a persisted trade row with a placement and a frozen owner and a null outcome -- the direct opposite of the clause's 'a thing whose only reports are withdrawals was never held at all'. That is the sharpest concrete violation the answer creates and it is why three trade-lifecycle groups move. (3) positions is as described: holding_change.sql's latest_report filter is (cdc_flag IS NULL OR cdc_flag IN ('I','U')), so a D-only pair already produces no row; what changes there is the any-D whole-pair abstention in the completeness audit. FINDINGS ON THE CLAUSE ITSELF, both worth more than any verdict above. (a) L1.deletion-withdraws and L1.owner-standing are in tension and neither yields: owner-standing says an account's standing includes its owner's standing at the same moment, and deletion-withdraws says a withdrawn customer has no standing from its moment forward. An account that stands while its owning customer is withdrawn therefore has a standing that includes a non-existent standing. The clause does not say whether the account's as-of answer also becomes no-answer (withdrawal propagating down the ownership edge, which would contradict 'a withdrawal creates nothing... it neither opens nor closes an account' only weakly), or whether the account answers with a null owner half (which is the CE's own named tempting-wrong-repair, an answer where there is none), or whether withdrawing a customer with standing accounts is itself a reportable violation. Recommend a CE before ownership-history recompiles; until then sg.owner-standing has no projectable rule for the case and must hold it. (b) the clause is written entirely in as-of language ('a question asked as of that moment or later has no answer'), but logical.trade and logical.holding_change are not as-of-able -- they are single current rows with no effective_from. 'From its moment forward the record has no standing' therefore has no literal reading for a withdrawn trade that earlier stood: nothing in the clause says whether such a trade's row keeps reporting its last outcome, or must stop answering. sg.outcome is kept on the reading that the row stands as history, which is the reading the clause's own 'stands as history' sentence supports for holdings; if the business means a withdrawn trade must stop answering, that is a new element and this keep must be revisited. (c) no received record carries a D flag anywhere, so no re-projection can produce received evidence for any of this: every invalidate above must be discharged against the labeled constructed withdrawal scenario the CE's deterministic assertion already specifies, and the D-only case needs a second constructed scenario the CE does not specify (a withdrawal of a record the brokerage does NOT already have, which L1.constructed-scenarios' second sentence arguably forbids a constructed scenario from introducing). That tension is worth naming in the same CE as (a). Jev p values are the ten medium-band scores in evidence/jev/calls.jsonl at ts 1789678671-1789678677; per-group attribution is by call order and is indicative, not asserted.
